clue.text: Archetypal bachelor pressed by heartless adversary on show

indicators.note: a thing without a heart has lost its centre, so the middle letter goes

parts.note: to prove something is to show it

indicators.note: something pressed by another is squeezed between its sides, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: RIVAL with its central V removed
B is the standard abbreviation for bachelor

explanation.surface: A stereotypical bachelor is being pursued by a determined rival in public.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, 'on' means placed after, so the bachelor-in-rival piece follows the word for show.
explanation.definitionFit: Something proverbial is so well known it serves as the archetype or textbook example of its kind.

clue.text: Regularly applying product gives you seductive look

indicators.note: applying a regular rule means taking letters at even intervals, every other one

parts.note: first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: Applying a cosmetic product such as lipstick every day is supposed to make you look alluring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Applying product' reads as make-up instructions, but 'Regularly' picks every other letter of 'product'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pushing the lips forward is a classic come-hither expression used by models and flirts alike.

clue.text: Balls-up in Middlesbrough!

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading the letters from bottom to top
the letters sit inside the following word rather than standing for anything

parts.note: fifth to eighth letters of the town's name

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a mess-up, a cock-up, happening in the northern English town of Middlesbrough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Balls-up' is British slang for a blunder, but the hyphen hides a split: 'Balls' is the definition and 'up' the direction signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Orbs are spheres, and balls are spherical objects, so the two words are plain synonyms.

clue.text: Chagrin of former primate maintaining small allotment

parts.note: ex- means former

indicators.note: to maintain is to hold on to, so one piece holds another inside it

parts.note: an ape is a primate
S is the abbreviation for small
a ration is an allotted share

explanation.surface: An ex-archbishop is annoyed about keeping a tiny vegetable patch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Former primate' tempts you towards an ex-archbishop, since an archbishop is a primate of the Church; here the primate is an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name a feeling of annoyed frustration or vexation when things go badly.

clue.text: Empty pool bordering lake

indicators.note: to border something is to run around its edges, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: a bank is a pool of money or stakes, as in a gambling game
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A drained swimming pool sits right next to a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pool' looks like water beside the lake, but it is the pool of money held by a bank.
explanation.definitionFit: A blank page or stare is an empty one, with nothing written or shown in it.

clue.text: American is catching on, following everybody's hints

indicators.note: to catch something is to take hold of it, so one piece goes inside another
coming after means the next pieces are placed behind what follows

parts.note: all means everybody; the 's just joins
US is short for American
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An American picks up on everyone's subtle suggestions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catching on' reads as understanding, but the phrase splits: 'catching' is the container signal and 'on' is its own piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An allusion is an indirect reference or suggestion, so allusions are hints rather than direct statements.

clue.text: Join main motorway

parts.note: the main is an old poetic term for the open sea
British motorways are numbered M1, M25 and so on

explanation.surface: An instruction to merge onto the principal motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Join main motorway' sounds like driving directions; 'main' is the sea, as in the Spanish Main.
explanation.definitionFit: A seam is the line where two pieces of fabric or material are stitched together, a joint.

clue.text: Self-important GI locates bombs planted around island

indicators.note: a thing planted around another encloses it, so one piece sits inside
a bombed site is blown apart, so the letters are scattered into new positions

parts.note: taken as written, as fodder
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A pompous American soldier finds explosive devices that someone has hidden on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bombs' looks like a noun but is a verb here; a GI is an American soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: An egoistical person is full of their own importance and thinks mainly about themselves.

clue.text: Physician, broken by stay in A&E, feigned illness

indicators.note: something broken by another is split open with the other wedged into the gap

parts.note: MD, Doctor of Medicine

indicators.note: being inside something means sitting between its letters

parts.note: the two letters as printed
to linger is to stay on

explanation.surface: A doctor, exhausted by a long shift in Accident and Emergency, pretended to be sick.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E is the British hospital emergency department; the clue uses only its two letters, which wrap the stay before the physician is broken open.
explanation.definitionFit: To malinger is to pretend to be unwell, typically to dodge work, so the past tense matches.

clue.text: Terribly posh area besieged by disorderly rabble entering city

parts.note: U means upper-class, as in U and non-U

indicators.note: a place besieged is surrounded on all sides, so one piece goes inside another
to enter is to go inside, so the group goes into the next piece

parts.note: NY, New York

indicators.note: something disorderly is out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for area
taken as written, as fodder

explanation.surface: A smart neighbourhood under siege by an unruly mob invading the city would be a terrible thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terribly' looks like an anagram signal, but it is the definition; the area letter joins the mob before the shuffle, which is why 'besieged' comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Unbearably and terribly are both intensifying adverbs meaning to an intolerable or extreme degree.

clue.text: Jay bird's prominent feature

parts.note: the sound of the letter's spoken name, jay, gives the letter J
an owl is a bird

explanation.surface: Asks what the most striking feature of a jay, the bird, is.
explanation.walkthrough: Jay looks like the bird, but it is the name of a letter; the bird is the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy jowl, the fleshy lower jaw or cheek, is a conspicuous facial characteristic.

clue.text: Classification code originally adopted by old Beijing religious community

indicators.note: something adopted is taken in, so one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: the former Western name for China's capital

indicators.note: the original part of a word is its start, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: its opening letter
a religious order, such as of monks or nuns

explanation.surface: A classification code first taken up by an ancient religious group in Beijing.
explanation.walkthrough: Peking was the usual English name for Beijing until the 1980s, hence 'old'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pecking order is a hierarchy of rank, a ranking or classification of who stands above whom.

clue.text: Representative keeps fighting with sponsor

indicators.note: things that are fighting are thrown about and tangled up, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written, as fodder
taken as written, as fodder

explanation.surface: A delegate is constantly quarrelling with the backer who funds them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeps fighting' reads as one phrase, but 'keeps' is fodder joined with 'sponsor', and 'fighting' mixes the letters of both.
explanation.definitionFit: A spokesperson speaks on behalf of a group or organisation, acting as its representative.

clue.text: Rookies putting location before brass

indicators.note: coming before means placed in front, setting the order of the pieces

parts.note: a green is a place, such as a village green
horns are brass instruments

explanation.surface: Novice golfers practising their putting near the expensive items, or recruits who rank place ahead of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting' suggests a golf putting green, which nudges towards the first part; 'brass' looks like money or officers but is the instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean inexperienced newcomers, people new to a job or activity.

clue.text: Like Pepys, essentially, diarist cultivated houseplant

parts.note: as means like

indicators.note: cultivated ground is worked over and turned, so the letters are rearranged
the essence of something is its core, so only the central letter is kept

parts.note: the middle letter of the five-letter name
taken as written, as fodder

explanation.surface: Samuel Pepys, the famous diarist, supposedly grew a particular house plant.
explanation.walkthrough: Pepys was a 17th-century English diarist, which makes 'diarist' feel like description rather than fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The aspidistra is a hardy leafy plant long popular as an indoor pot plant in British homes.

clue.text: Playful creature finally brought teacher back for coffee

indicators.note: going back means travelling the wrong way, so the letters read in reverse

parts.note: otters are famously playful animals

indicators.note: the final part of a word is its end, so only its last letter is kept

parts.note: its final letter
schoolchildren address a male teacher as sir

explanation.surface: A playful animal finally brought the teacher a coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: OTTER, T and SIR are joined and then the whole string is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A ristretto is a very short, concentrated shot of espresso, a type of Italian coffee.

clue.text: Hearing about hollow triumph over Norway in competition

indicators.note: something hollow has its inside scooped out, so only the outer letters remain
about means around, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: a court hearing is a trial
the word with all but its outer letters removed
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over
N is the international vehicle code for Norway

explanation.surface: A legal hearing about an empty victory over Norway in an international contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearing' suggests a sound clue, but here it is a court hearing; the hollowed triumph keeps just its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A triathlon is an endurance sporting contest combining swimming, cycling and running in sequence.

clue.text: One pursuing Grand Knight with iron weapon

indicators.note: one who pursues comes behind, so this piece is placed after the others

parts.note: a grand is a thousand, and K stands for a thousand
N is the chess notation for a knight
I is the Roman numeral one
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: Someone chasing a Grand Knight armed with an iron weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: Grand gives K via a thousand, as in a salary of 50K.
explanation.definitionFit: A knife is a bladed tool that can be used as a weapon for stabbing or cutting.

clue.text: Throw out scientist's conclusion after artifice is discovered

indicators.note: dis-covered means with its cover taken off, so the outer letters go
coming after means placed behind, which fixes the order of the pieces

parts.note: DEVICE, a trick or ruse, without its first and last letters

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A scientist's findings are thrown out once trickery comes to light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is discovered' sounds like exposure of fraud; read as 'dis-covered', it strips DEVICE to its inner letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To evict is to expel a tenant or occupant from a property, forcing them out.

clue.text: Enrage four couples when speaking out?

indicators.note: what we hear when words are spoken can be spelt differently from how they sound

parts.note: to incense someone is to enrage them
four pairs make eight

explanation.surface: Asks whether you would annoy four pairs of people by speaking up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speaking out' looks like one phrase meaning protest; the definition is just the last word, 'out'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is out cold is unconscious, lacking all physical sensation or awareness, which is what insensate means.

clue.text: Foolishly forget Idaho contains hospital providing cure for alcoholics?

indicators.note: something that contains another holds it inside
acting foolishly means behaving without sense, so the letters lose their order

parts.note: taken as written, as fodder
H is the map sign for hospital

explanation.surface: Silly to overlook the fact that Idaho has a hospital treating heavy drinkers.
explanation.walkthrough: H goes into the fodder before the whole lot is mixed. The question mark flags a loose definition, since this remedy is for hangovers.
explanation.definitionFit: The hair of the dog is a further alcoholic drink taken as a supposed remedy for a hangover.

clue.text: Supply Ecstasy and crack

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
a crack is a witty remark

explanation.surface: A drug dealer's instruction to provide two illegal drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' sits beside Ecstasy as a drug, but it is a wisecrack.
explanation.definitionFit: To equip is to provide someone with what they need, to furnish or kit them out.

clue.text: Revolutionary outfit show off

indicators.note: a revolution turns something right round, so the letters face the other way

parts.note: garb is clothing, an outfit

explanation.surface: A radical new set of clothes worn to impress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary outfit' suggests a rebel group; 'outfit' is clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To brag is to boast about yourself, which is how one shows off.

clue.text: God of childhood innocence

indicators.note: of means taken from, so the letters come from within the following words

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Names a deity who presides over the innocence of children.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase reads like a divine title, but the god's name runs across the join of the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Odin is the chief deity of Norse mythology, father of Thor.

clue.text: Hotelier picked up court orders

indicators.note: to pick up a sound is to hear it, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: writs are formal orders issued by a court

explanation.surface: A hotel owner was served with legal injunctions.
explanation.walkthrough: César Ritz was the Swiss hotelier who founded the Ritz hotels in Paris and London.
explanation.definitionFit: César Ritz was a famous Swiss hotel founder, so his surname names a hotelier.

clue.text: Creator of institution admits liberal journalist struggled

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: the founder creates an institution
L is the abbreviation for Liberal
ED, an editor

explanation.surface: The founder of an organisation lets in a left-leaning reporter who had a hard time.
explanation.walkthrough: ED, short for editor, is the crossword's stock journalist.
explanation.definitionFit: To flounder is to struggle clumsily, whether physically in water or mentally with a task.

clue.text: Howl about disappearing trick

indicators.note: what disappears is no longer there, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: to scream is to howl
re means about or concerning; these letters are the ones removed

explanation.surface: A cry of protest at a vanishing act by a magician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disappearing trick' looks like a magic act; 'trick' is the definition and 'disappearing' acts on 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: A scam is a dishonest scheme or swindle, a trick to cheat someone.

clue.text: Perennial problem keeps retired secretary and doctor working

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so one piece holds others inside

parts.note: a snag is a problem

indicators.note: to retire is to go back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: PA, personal assistant
DR is short for doctor
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A recurring difficulty: a doctor and a secretary who should have retired keep working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perennial problem' reads as one phrase, but 'Perennial' alone is the definition, a plant that lives for years.
explanation.definitionFit: The snapdragon, or antirrhinum, is a garden flower often grown as a perennial plant.
